brands.d: Five-generation Tokyo knife house founded by Minosuke Matsuzawa; hongasumi single-bevel knives and the KS wa-gyuto are references.
Family-owned Seki maker, Japan's oldest Western-style knife maker; all production in-house, Swedish steels.
Hand-forging workshop founded 1920, in Niimi since 1951; third-generation smith Shosui Takeda forges tall, thin Aogami Super blades.
All-steel knife brand of Yoshida Metal Industry (Yoshikin), Tsubame; Komin Yamada's 1983 design with dimpled sand-filled handles in CROMOVA 18.
Kai Group's Western-market brand launched 2002, made in Seki; VG-MAX cores under Damascus cladding and PakkaWood handles.
eras: Kai Group (founded Seki 1908 by Saijiro Endo)

brands.d: Tsubame-Sanjo maker (Fujitora) founded 1953; DP three-layer VG10 line is the global entry point to Japanese knives, plus traditional Shirogami single-bevels.
Brand of Aoki Hamono Seisakusho (founded 1947 as Aoki Ichiro Shoten, Sakai office 1963) selling Sakai-forged single-bevel and Western knives across many lines.
Sakai workshop known for exceptionally thin grinds and fit-and-finish across HD2, GS+, SLD and hand-forged Fujiyama lines.
Maker of the Ginga line: very light, thin Swedish-stainless and carbon knives with octagonal magnolia handles.
Forge founded in Sanjo in 1964 by Tokifusa Iizuka, now run by his sons; hand-forged, stone-ground kasumi and kitaeji knives with long waiting lists.
Fourth-generation Sanjo forge (Yamamoto) hammer-forging thin nashiji knives in SKD semi-stainless and White #2.
Sanjo maker of hand-forged home and professional knives since 1948; Hocho Kobo and Bocho Kobo ranges, clad Aogami and SLD.
Seki manufacturer whose MV-H molybdenum-vanadium stainless 'honyaki' range is a professional staple.
Founded 1560 by Fujiwara Aritsugu, former Imperial sword supplier turned knife maker; one of the world's oldest companies, 18 generations.
Forge in Yatsushiro, Kumamoto, with a lineage traced to the 13th century; Aogami Super kurouchi knives at HRC 64–65.
Echizen maker known for grinding SG2/R2 powder-steel blades extremely thin at modest prices.
Smith whose Denka (Aogami Super) and Maboroshi lines are prized for heat treatment and edge retention despite rustic finish.

traditions.d: Government-designated forged-blade craft: hand-forged, clay-quenched single-bevel knives made under a division of labour between smith, sharpener and handle fitter.
traditions.tech: forge-welding steel to soft iron at ~900 °C, hand hammering, clay-coated water quench, hand sharpening and finishing
traditions.mat: carbon steel (shirogami, aogami) on soft iron; magnolia handles with buffalo-horn ferrules
traditions.auth: Sakai smith and sharpener marks; Tokugawa-era 'gokuin' quality stamp heritage; kasumi/hongasumi finish with urasuki hollow back

traditions.d: Sword-making city since swordsmith Motoshige settled there; today Japan's volume centre for machine-forged stainless Western-style knives finished by hand.
traditions.tech: machine stamping/forging and quenching, hand sharpening and handle fitting
traditions.mat: stainless and powder steels (VG10, VG-MAX, molybdenum-vanadium), Swedish steels
traditions.auth: 'Seki Japan' marks; Kai, Misono, Masahiro house stamps

traditions.d: 700-year forged-blade tradition begun by Kyoto swordsmith Chiyozuru Kuniyasu making sickles; designated traditional craft, now centred on Takefu Knife Village.
traditions.tech: hand forging of agricultural-tool heritage, prized toughness
traditions.auth: Echizen Uchihamono Cooperative designation; maker mei from Takefu smiths

traditions.d: Free-forged working blades from Shikoku's forestry and farming country: axes, sickles, hoes and rustic kurouchi kitchen knives in carbon steel.
traditions.tech: free forging without moulds, hand hammering, kurouchi finish
traditions.auth: rustic hand-forged kurouchi finish; Tosa cooperative labelling

traditions.r: Tsubame and Sanjo, Niigata Prefecture, Japan
traditions.d: Metalworking region begun with nails and farm hardware; Tsubame excels in precision stainless engineering, Sanjo in traditional hand forging.
traditions.tech: Tsubame: stamping and precision stainless; Sanjo: hammer forging, nashiji and kurouchi finishes
traditions.mat: stainless (CROMOVA, VG10), SKD/SLD semi-stainless, shirogami, aogami
traditions.auth: maker mei; Sanjo forges' hand-ground finishes vs Tsubame machine precision

traditions.d: Japan's oldest carpentry-tool region; chisel and plane-blade steel skills carried into small-volume kitchen knife making.
traditions.tech: hand forging from carpentry-tool tradition, disciplined geometry and heat treatment

notes: Shelf 'Japanese knives' rebuilt: 9 kinds (Gyuto, Santoku, Nakiri, Bunka, Kiritsuke, Honesuki, Usuba, Yanagiba, Deba), 31 archetypes, 17 brands, 6 traditions. Old kinds k20 Santoku, k21 Nakiri, k23 Usuba, k24 Yanagiba, k25 Deba carried over; old Tojiro Shirogami Usuba model became a version. Dropped: Wüsthof Classic Ikon and Eden Classic Damast/Dento ranges (German/retailer house-brand range spam on Japanese-shape kinds; Wüsthof belongs with Western knives). Takeda Hamono is in Niimi, Okayama (not Tosa as the brief said) per the retrieved maker page; kept as a gyuto/bunka archetype but not listed under Tosa. Archetype years are 'n.d.' where no retrieved page gives a launch date; maker founding years given instead. Not added for lack of a retrieved page: Masamoto Tsukiji, Hitohira, Sakai Jikko, Yoshihiro, Hinoura, Kato/Yoshimi (Takefu), Motokyuichi, Tsukasa (Miki), Masahiro MV-H santoku (kept only as a loose model). Steel and construction attributes are types ('t') on each kind, not separate kinds. Takohiki/fuguhiki, kamagata/edo usuba, ko-deba/mioroshi, garasuki/hankotsu are types per the plan. The wiki/wikidata helper tools errored (lock-file directory), so all Wikipedia sources were retrieved via web_fetch after web_search.
